title: Your cost floor, the market range and the value you create
course_title: Pricing & Value Strategy for Services and Digital Work

say: Your cost floor, the market range, and the value you create.
This is the video for Module 1 of Pricing and Value Strategy.
With a service, your biggest cost is invisible: your hours. For example, Chiamaka and Bisi are designers in Enugu, with similar skill and about 80 paid hours a month.
Chiamaka charges 15,000 naira a logo, because a client once called it normal. Each logo takes 10 hours, so she earns just 1,500 naira an hour.

panel.heading: Same skill, same hours, different pay

say: Bisi sells a brand starter pack for 60,000 naira. It takes 16 hours, so she earns 3,750 naira an hour, and 180,000 naira more each month.
The difference is not talent. Bisi priced on purpose. That number, money received divided by all the hours the job really took, is your effective hourly rate.

panel.heading: Same skill, same hours, different pay

say: The cost floor is the lowest price that still pays your living needs, your business costs and a small buffer. Below it, you are paying the client to work for them.

panel.heading: Where every price sits
items: Value ceiling: what it is worth to the client

say: The market range is what comparable providers charge for comparable work. It shows what buyers are used to, not what you must charge.

panel.heading: Where every price sits
items: Value ceiling: what it is worth to the client

say: The value ceiling is what the result is worth to this client, such as more sales or hours saved.
Choose a price above your floor, sensible for your market, and clearly below the value the client expects. Then both of you win.

panel.heading: Where every price sits
items: Value ceiling: what it is worth to the client

say: Now calculate your floor. Start with a monthly money target.
Zainab needs 220,000 naira a month in personal pay. Always put your own pay first.
Her business costs are 90,000 naira: data, generator fuel, software, transport, and a fund to replace her laptop and phone.
She adds a 15% buffer for savings, slow months and tax.
Her monthly target is 356,500 naira.
Only billable hours earn money. Zainab works 160 hours a month, but tracking one week showed only 55% was billable. That is 88 hours.
356,500 naira divided by 88 hours, rounded up, is 4,100 naira per hour. That is her floor.
Her current package is 12 posts a month, which takes about 14 hours.
So its floor price is 14 times 4,100. That is 57,400 naira.
She charges 40,000 naira. She is 17,400 naira short on every client who buys it.
Non-billable time, like quotes, admin and chasing payments, is real work nobody pays for directly. So divide by billable hours only.

panel.heading: From target to floor price
panel.rule: Divide by billable hours, not all hours. Round up, never down.

say: Collect at least five rates from peers, public rate cards and platforms.

panel.heading: Compare like with like
items: Collect at least five real rates
Convert to one unit, such as per post
Sort them and find the middle value

say: Note what each includes, because a cheap offer with no revisions is a different product.

panel.heading: Compare like with like
items: Collect at least five real rates
Convert to one unit, such as per post
Sort them and find the middle value

say: Convert each to one unit. Zainab's five offers ranged from 2,333 to 5,000 naira per post.

panel.heading: Compare like with like
items: Collect at least five real rates
Convert to one unit, such as per post
Sort them and find the middle value

say: The middle value was 4,000 naira per post, so 48,000 naira for 12 posts. Her floor of 57,400 is near the top, so she must show extra value, like reports and faster replies. The cheapest price in a WhatsApp group is not the market price.

say: Pricing is wasted if you are not paid. Payment alerts and screenshots can be faked, so confirm money in your own banking app.
If a client overpays and asks for a refund of the difference, wait until the full amount is settled. And no genuine client needs your OTP, PIN or login code.

panel.heading: Before you deliver work
items: Deposit confirmed in your banking app
